nodes.statement: For unbiased binary states, H(X)=1 bit.
For N unbiased binary elements, S_info = N k_B ln 2 under the source's Omega construction.
Under the source erasure model, Delta S_info = -N k_B ln 2.
Landauer erasure under the relevant thermodynamic assumptions has a minimum dissipation/work scale k_B T ln 2 per lost bit.
The p.2 printed inequality direction for the physical-entropy/heat term conflicts with the immediately preceding second-law balance and conventional lower-bound form.
A stored bit has intrinsic energy E_bit = k_B T ln 2 while information is stored.
nodes.source_locator: p.2 Section II leading to Eq.(6)

nodes.statement: If E_bit is an ordinary stored energy contribution, mass-energy equivalence gives m_bit = E_bit/c^2.
Conditional on MEI-N6 and MEI-N7, m_bit = k_B T ln 2 / c^2.
At 300 K, m_bit is about 3.19e-38 kg and a decimal 1 TB device changes by about 2.5e-25 kg between erased and full-information states.

edges.note: The erasure lower bound does not by itself identify the stored state's intrinsic energy.
